featured_reviews.name: Darren Talati
featured_reviews.review_text:
Before you waste your time and money, read this. Five minutes now could save you from months of regret.

If negative stars were an option, Exemplar Dot Space would get them all. Our experience with this firm has been nothing short of a scam wrapped in fake promises and zero accountability.

False Promises, Fake Deadlines & Endless Excuses:
Our project started in July with a promised completion by Diwali. Then came December, Christmas, mid-Jan, mid-Feb, and now it’s March—with only 70% of the house completed. Every single deadline was given by them, yet missed with excuse after excuse—workers unavailable, vendor delays, production issues, "aa jayega." The only thing that ever "came" was another round of lies and stalling tactics.

Modular Disaster – A Joke of Execution:
We were assured that modular furniture would be the best finish with fast execution. What a joke. Nine months later, our modular is still incomplete. We took 8 separate deliveries, yet the shutters arrived in the wrong sizes—we needed 8ft shutters, they sent 7ft ones. How do you even mess up something this basic? Every single plank and shutter is damaged and their response? "Sab replace ho jayega." Sure, just like everything else they promised.

Istekhar, the so-called person in charge (also one of the directors), would ignore messages for days, only to show up virtually at 11-11:30pm. Excuse me? I’m a paying client, not your friend. Treat us with some professionalism.

Financial Exploitation – Holding Work Hostage for Money:
Despite never delaying a single payment, we were constantly told vendors weren’t paid. Then in end-February, during a meeting, Istekhar straight-up said:
"Ma’am, if you don’t give payment, work will slow down, nothing else."
Excuse me? We had already overpaid for unfinished work, yet this was the attitude we got. This is when we sensed something sus and put our foot down. This wasn’t a project anymore—we were being used like an ATM machine.

Internal Chaos & Unprofessionalism:
So apparently they subcontracted vendors who weren’t paid, so they stopped working. Then a new team showed up, leading to a literal argument between the old and new teams ON OUR SITE. My house is not a war zone, but these people turned it into one.

The "project manager" was totally clueless, making us run to buy materials as basic as glue for LED strips. Meanwhile, the people who pitched the project—Devi and Pratik—vanished after the first meeting. Istekhar showed up only when payments were due—convenient, isn’t it?

Final Straw – The Last Big Lie:
When we drove them out in frustration, Istekhar suddenly claimed that all the modular furniture was ready for delivery THAT day. Oh really? Then we asked for the delivery the next day. Nothing came. No calls. No response. What a shameless, efficient, emotionless lie. They knew we had already paid, so why bother delivering?

Final Words – Your Dream Home Deserves Better:
A dream home is not just a structure—it’s a lifetime of planning, savings, and emotions. It’s supposed to be a place of joy, not a battlefield of broken promises, delays, and financial stress. Exemplar Dot Space robbed us of that experience, turning what should have been a beautiful journey into nine months of frustration and regret.

Oh, and I’m sure if the team reads this, they’ll have a brand-new excuse ready—probably something like “The client didn’t let us complete the project.” Right, because clearly, I should’ve just handed you a five-year lease on my unfinished house for a 1000 sq. ft. job with no bathrooms or civil work. Maybe I should’ve also thrown in a spa day and a vacation so you could really take your time? Hilarious.
0/10 recommendation score.
